To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the content of nucleotide phosphoric acids in subcellular fraction of cow milk is determined by the intensity of the processes of the secretion and synthesis of milk components, that in the case of prolonged intervals between milkings there is a decrease in the activity of alkaline phospahatase in the cytoplasm and in the content of nucleotides in the cell-nuclear fraction and mitochondrial fraction, and that the intensity of the synthesis of nucleotides is determined by the activity of alkalne
the nucleic acid content of the subcellular fraction of milk is dependent on the interval between milkings.
the nucleic acid content in the mitochondrial and nuclear fractions decreases in milk in different time intervals between milkings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using subcellular fractions for studying the secretory processes and the functional condition of the udder.
the possibility of using the content of nucleotide phosphorus and activity of alkalide phosphatase as the criteria of the intensity of the mammary gland function in dairy cows.
the possibility of using the nucleic acids and phosphoric compounds as the indicators of the intensity of the mammary secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nucleic acids are the most important component of the subcellular particles of milk and the content of the nucleic acids in these fractions is the most sensitive indicator of the secretory activity of the mammary gland.
the nucleic acids content in the cell nuclear fraction and in the mitochondrial fraction of cow milk decreases with the increase in the interval between milkings.
the nucleic acid content in the mitochondrial and cell nuclear fractions of cow milk is not constant and depends on the interval between milkings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the milk of cows with prolonged intervals between milkings the intensity of the nucleic acids secretion decreases and the intensity of the alkaline phosphatases secretion rises.
a prolonged interval between milkings leads to a reduction of the intensity of the processes of synthesis of the phosphoric and nucleic compounds and of the secretion of the milk.

the content of nuclei and mitochondria in the cell fraction is higher in fresh milk than in the milk of the last milking of a day, that the content of the nucleic acids in these fractions is also higher and that the content of phosphates in milk of the first milking of the day is higher than in fresh milk.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the content of nucleotides in the subcellu- lar fractions and the intensity of the secretion of phosphoric compounds in milk are closely connected with the intensity of the processes of the milk synthesis and secretion in the mammary glands of cows.

the content of nucleotide in the mitochondrial fraction of cow milk is higher than that of the nuclear fraction, and that the content of these compounds is the highest in fresh milk and decreases with the prolongation of the time between milkings.
the nucleic acids content in the cell-nuclear fraction is higher than that in the mitochondrial fraction.
